feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 7 (0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 16 mm, y = 0.02 m) gave the best score (303.8) with 14 of 20 oval completions, but slalom line loss was 0.3 per run, against 0 at 0.8 kg in iteration 5. Iteration 5 (0.8 kg, same row and footprint) gave zero line loss on all tracks, so the footprint and row were not the cause on their own. The inertia change added the slalom loss. Iteration 6 showed that raising wheel radius cut oval progress (0.358 to 0.291), so speed is not the lever. Max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.064 m across geometry changes, but iteration 7 oval max_error was 0.048 on completing runs, so the failures are sharp-bend losses, not a general floor. Next race: if slalom line loss falls toward 0 with oval completions at or above about 14 of 20, keep 12 mm and move the s-bend and slalom effort to turn authority. If line loss does not fall, the outer span is the limit, so widen to x = ±0.07 m. If line loss rises with 12 mm, the footprint is too small to hold the edge sensors, so return to 16 mm and widen the span.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events stay at or above about 0.25 with 12 mm sensors (iteration 7 at 16 mm gave 0.3): widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.07 m at the same 0.02 m pitch, since iteration 5 at 0.8 kg with x = ±0.06 m and 16 mm gave zero losses only when inertia was higher, and the wider span gives the line more margin before the edge.

If oval completions fall below about 12 of 20 with 12 mm (iteration 7 gave 14 of 20 at 16 mm): return sensor_size to 0.016 m and keep the iteration 7 positions, since the 16 mm footprint is the only sensing change that produced oval completions.

If the s-bend and slalom still show no completion or progress above 0.5 after the footprint change: try wheel_track 0.11 m at 0.6 kg, since iteration 1 at 0.12 m with 0.8 kg had the lowest oscillation (0.173), and a wider track reduces yaw gain per command. Accept that this may lower oval progress, since iteration 2 at 0.09 m gave the highest progress (0.44).
